## Clean Chapel Hill and Jordan Lake bird counts

These steps create one CSV per location and season with `COMMON NAME` followed
by numeric year columns in chronological order. Durham files are not read or
modified. The original Excel files are preserved.

Only the annual count blocks are imported: the later year-labeled abundance
codes, summary statistics, survey effort, weather, dates, and notes are excluded.
Chapel Hill retains the main species lists, excluding the separate unidentified
and hybrid records and the winter list of rejected sightings. Jordan Lake keeps
its unidentified bird-count records as well as its named species.

Blank, `NA`, and `N/A` counts become zero. Chapel Hill's `cw` markers denote
count-week sightings rather than count-day totals and are also recorded as zero.
Other unexpected nonnumeric values raise an error instead of silently losing data.

```{r}
#| label: setup

# Install once if needed: install.packages("readxl")
library(readxl)

# Support both rendering from r-files/ and running from the repository root.
data_dir <- if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data" else "data"
stopifnot(dir.exists(data_dir))
```

## Shared cleaning functions

Read headers as data so Excel's duplicate year labels are not automatically
changed to names such as `1931...7`. The source ranges below are deliberately
limited to count columns; some abundance-code columns also have year headers.
Jordan Lake winter labels such as `1986-87` become `1986`.

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-functions

clean_counts <- function(file, sheet, header_row, last_column, bird_rows) {
  raw <- read_excel(
    file.path(data_dir, file), sheet = sheet,
    range = cell_limits(c(header_row, 1), c(max(bird_rows), last_column)),
    col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "minimal"
  )
  headers <- toupper(trimws(as.character(unlist(raw[1, ]))))
  name_column <- which(headers == "COMMON NAME")
  year_columns <- which(grepl("^[12][0-9]{3}(-([0-9]{2}|[0-9]{4}))?$", headers))
  stopifnot(length(name_column) == 1L, length(year_columns) > 0L)

  # The first year in these winter ranges is the lesser year.
  years <- sub("-.*$", "", headers[year_columns])
  birds <- as.data.frame(raw[bird_rows - header_row + 1L,
                            c(name_column, year_columns), drop = FALSE])
  names(birds) <- c("COMMON NAME", years)
  birds[[1]] <- trimws(birds[[1]])
  birds <- birds[!is.na(birds[[1]]) & birds[[1]] != "", , drop = FALSE]

  for (j in seq_along(years) + 1L) {
    values <- toupper(trimws(birds[[j]]))
    values[is.na(values) | values %in% c("", "NA", "N/A", "#N/A", "CW")] <- "0"
    counts <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(values))
    invalid <- !is.finite(counts) | counts < 0 | counts != floor(counts)
    if (any(invalid)) {
      stop("Invalid counts in ", file, " (", years[j - 1L], "): ",
           paste(unique(values[invalid]), collapse = ", "))
    }
    birds[[j]] <- counts
  }

  # Combine repeated year labels into a single annual count column.
  result <- data.frame(birds[[1]], check.names = FALSE)
  names(result) <- "COMMON NAME"
  for (year in sort(unique(years))) {
    columns <- which(years == year) + 1L
    result[[year]] <- rowSums(birds[, columns, drop = FALSE])
  }
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  stopifnot(!anyNA(result), !anyDuplicated(result[[1]]),
            identical(names(result), toupper(names(result))))
  result
}
```

## Chapel Hill

The spring species block is Excel rows 5–227 and the winter species block is
rows 4–168. Later rows contain hybrids, unidentified birds, totals, effort, or
notes. The winter source has two columns labeled `1931`; their counts are summed
into a single `1931` column without guessing a replacement year.

```{r}
#| label: clean-chapel-hill

chapel_hill_spring <- clean_counts(
  "spring/Chapel-Hill-1952-2024-spring.xlsx", "CHBCSC",
  header_row = 4, last_column = 70, bird_rows = 5:227
)
chapel_hill_winter <- clean_counts(
  "winter/Chapel-Hill-1923-2023-winter.xlsx", "Sheet1",
  header_row = 3, last_column = 96, bird_rows = 4:168
)
```

## Jordan Lake

Spring species occupy rows 5–230; additional unidentified bird counts occupy
rows 242–266, after the summary and effort rows. Winter bird counts occupy
rows 5–177, before the summary rows. The winter range `2021-22` becomes `2021`,
so the cleaned winter year columns run from 1977 through 2021.

```{r}
#| label: clean-jordan-lake

jordan_lake_spring <- clean_counts(
  "spring/Jordan-Lake-1977-2022-spring.xlsx", "JLSBC",
  header_row = 4, last_column = 49, bird_rows = c(5:230, 242:266)
)
jordan_lake_winter <- clean_counts(
  "winter/Jordan-Lake-1977-2022-winter.xlsx", "JLCBC",
  header_row = 4, last_column = 48, bird_rows = 5:177
)
```

## Validate and export

Rendering this document writes the four cleaned CSVs beside their source files.
Year columns contain numeric counts only, with no missing values or row-number
column. These ranges should be reviewed if the source spreadsheets change.

```{r}
#| label: validate-and-export

cleaned <- list(
  "spring/chapel_hill_spring_final.csv" = chapel_hill_spring,
  "winter/chapel_hill_winter_final.csv" = chapel_hill_winter,
  "spring/jordan_lake_spring_final.csv" = jordan_lake_spring,
  "winter/jordan_lake_winter_final.csv" = jordan_lake_winter
)

for (file in names(cleaned)) {
  counts <- cleaned[[file]]
  stopifnot(
    names(counts)[1] == "COMMON NAME",
    all(grepl("^[12][0-9]{3}$", names(counts)[-1])),
    !anyDuplicated(names(counts)),
    all(vapply(counts[-1], is.numeric, logical(1))),
    !anyNA(counts)
  )
  write.csv(counts, file.path(data_dir, file), row.names = FALSE, na = "0")
}

data.frame(
  DATASET = names(cleaned),
  BIRDS = vapply(cleaned, nrow, integer(1)),
  YEARS = vapply(cleaned, function(x) ncol(x) - 1L, integer(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```
